## Statement

Given integers $N\ge1$, even $M\ge2$, and $0\le y<M$, let $z=N\sin^2(\pi y/M)$. There is a terminating deterministic rational-interval procedure that produces an integer $q$ with $|q-z|\le2/3$. Its arithmetic work is a classical bit cost; no polynomial bit bound is asserted.

## Definition

If $y=0$, return $q=0$ exactly. Otherwise, for $r=4,5,\ldots$, compute
$$R_r=8^{2r+2}/(2r+2)!,\qquad D_r=\sum_{k=1}^r2k\,8^{2k-1}/(2k)!.$$
Continue to the next $r$ while $NR_r\ge1/24$. For the first remaining $r$, refine a rational enclosure $J$ of $\pi$ using [F1] until the propagated argument interval for $x=2\pi y/M$ has midpoint $x_r$ and radius $\rho_r$ with $ND_r\rho_r<1/24-NR_r$. Evaluate
$$C_r(x_r)=\sum_{k=0}^r(-1)^k x_r^{2k}/(2k)!.$$
For $0\le x<8$, the omitted cosine terms decrease for $k\ge r$ because $64/((2k+2)(2k+1))<1$. The mean value theorem bounds the change in $C_r$ across the argument interval by $D_r\rho_r$, and the alternating-series remainder is bounded by $R_r$. Thus
$$[C_r(x_r)-D_r\rho_r-R_r,\ C_r(x_r)+D_r\rho_r+R_r]$$
is a rational enclosure of $\cos x$. Convert it to a rational interval $I_r$ for $z=N(1-\cos x)/2$. Stop when $I_r$ has width less than $1/6$, and output the least integer $q$ whose closed radius-$2/3$ interval contains all of $I_r$; the integer is found by rational ceiling arithmetic.
